title: Steve Bannon Pleads Guilty in State Fraud Case, Avoids Jail
synopsis: On February 11, 2025, Trump ally Steve Bannon pleaded guilty in Manhattan state court to a single felony count of scheme to defraud for his role in the 'We Build the Wall' charity fraud, in which he and co-conspirators diverted more than $15 million in donor funds meant to build a southern border wall. He was sentenced to a three-year conditional discharge with no prison time. Manhattan DA Alvin Bragg had pursued the state charges after Trump pardoned Bannon in the final hours of his first term in January 2021, since presidential pardons only cover federal crimes. Two other defendants in the same scheme — Brian Kolfage and Andrew Badolato — had already been sentenced to prison; Bannon faced zero incarceration despite a felony conviction.

sources.title: Steve Bannon pleads guilty and avoids jail time in border wall fraud case : NPR

title: DOJ Orders Eric Adams Charges Dropped in Quid Pro Quo for Immigration Cooperation
synopsis: On February 10, 2025, acting Deputy AG Emil Bove sent a two-page memo ordering Manhattan prosecutors to immediately drop corruption charges against New York City Mayor Eric Adams, who had been indicted for accepting $100,000 in luxury travel from Turkish nationals. Bove stated the dismissal was not based on evidence but because the case was interfering with Adams' ability to assist in Trump's immigration crackdown. Adams' attorneys had allegedly proposed at a January 31 meeting that Adams would be in a position to 'assist with the Department's enforcement priorities only if the indictment were dismissed.' Six senior DOJ and SDNY prosecutors resigned in protest; the case was ultimately dismissed on February 14 after a career prosecutor filed the motion to spare his colleagues from being fired.

sources.title: Top Justice Department official orders prosecutors to drop charges against New York Mayor Eric Adams | AP News

title: Danielle Sassoon and Six Prosecutors Resign Rather Than Drop Adams Charges
synopsis: On February 13, 2025, acting SDNY U.S. Attorney Danielle Sassoon — a conservative Republican who clerked for Justice Antonin Scalia — resigned rather than comply with the order to drop the Adams indictment, sending a 6-page letter to AG Bondi declaring she was 'confident that Adams has committed the crimes with which he was charged.' Sassoon's letter explicitly stated that Adams' attorneys had proposed a quid pro quo and that the dismissal was 'driven by improper considerations.' Five other senior DOJ officials resigned the same day, including the two leaders of DOJ's Public Integrity Section in Washington when the case was transferred there. Career prosecutor Ed Sullivan ultimately filed the dismissal motion to spare remaining colleagues from being fired.

sources.title: Danielle Sassoon: Flurry of resignations after DOJ tells prosecutors to drop Eric Adams case

title: DOJ Purges Hundreds of FBI Agents Who Worked Jan. 6 or Trump Investigations
synopsis: On January 31, 2025, acting Deputy AG Emil Bove issued memos firing at least eight senior FBI executives and ordering a sweeping review of all FBI employees who had worked on January 6 or Trump-related investigations — potentially affecting thousands of agents. About two dozen prosecutors at the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office were terminated. The FBI Agents Association issued a rare public warning that hundreds of firings were coming. By June 2025, Kash Patel had pushed out senior FBI agents with decades of institutional knowledge, disbanded the premier public corruption unit, and reoriented the entire bureau toward immigration enforcement, while agents were subjected to expanded polygraph testing to identify leakers.

sources.title: Trump DOJ demands list of thousands of FBI agents, others who worked on Jan. 6 and Trump investigations for possible firing | CNN Politics

title: DOJ Drops Police Consent Decrees for Minneapolis, Louisville, Eight Other Cities
synopsis: On May 21, 2025, the DOJ Civil Rights Division — led by Harmeet Dhillon — announced it was dismissing pending lawsuits and proposed consent decrees against the Minneapolis and Louisville police departments, as well as closing investigations into six additional departments: Phoenix, Trenton, Memphis, Mount Vernon (NY), Oklahoma City, and Louisiana State Police. The Minneapolis and Louisville decrees had been negotiated following the police killings of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor respectively. Dhillon characterized the Biden-era investigations as relying on 'flawed methodologies' and 'wrongly equating statistical disparities with intentional discrimination.' Former DOJ Civil Rights Division chief Kristen Clarke called the rollback a 'patent disregard for our laws and the Constitution.'

title: DOJ Directs Investigations Into George Soros-Funded Progressive Prosecutors
synopsis: In May 2025, the DOJ Civil Rights Division opened an investigation into Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty over a policy directing prosecutors to consider racial disparities in plea negotiations. In September 2025, a DOJ senior official directed U.S. attorney's offices in at least seven states to prepare investigations into George Soros' Open Society Foundations on potential charges including material support for terrorism, arson, wire fraud, and racketeering — the directive following Trump and Vance publicly calling for Soros to be investigated. In May 2026, DOJ launched a civil rights probe into Fairfax County Commonwealth Attorney Steve Descano, who received over $600,000 from a Soros-funded PAC, over a policy of weighing immigration consequences in charging decisions.

title: Trump Threatens Insurrection Act Invocation Against Democratic Cities
synopsis: Beginning in October 2025, Trump repeatedly threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act of 1807 to deploy active-duty military troops into Chicago, Portland, and other Democratic-led cities over resistance to ICE operations. A federal judge in California had already ruled in September 2025 that the administration's deployment of active-duty troops to Los Angeles violated the Posse Comitatus Act of 1878. Senior White House aide Stephen Miller had been the leading internal proponent of invoking the Act, and officials shifted from debating whether to invoke it to how and when. Trump described anti-ICE protesters in Portland as committing 'pure insurrection,' while Illinois Gov. Pritzker accused Trump of deliberately manufacturing pretexts for military deployment against his political opponents.

title: DOJ Fires Over 139 Immigration Judges in Ongoing Purge
synopsis: Beginning February 15, 2025, the Trump administration started firing immigration judges without explanation, dismissing 20 in the first wave including 13 who had not yet been sworn in. Firings continued throughout the year: by October 2025, CNN reported 139 immigration judges had been fired, taken early-out offers, or been involuntarily transferred out of the approximately 700 nationwide. Analysis showed at least 30 dismissed judges had asylum grant rates of 30% or higher, suggesting a pattern of removing judges perceived as too lenient. The firings led to immigration case delays extending to 2029 and a growing backlog of nearly 4 million cases, even as Congress had authorized $3 billion to hire additional judges.

sources.title: Justice Department fires multiple immigration judges amid case backlog

title: Jack Smith Final Report: Evidence Was Sufficient to Convict Trump
synopsis: On January 14, 2025 — six days before Trump's inauguration — the Justice Department released Volume 1 of Special Counsel Jack Smith's 137-page final report on the election subversion investigation. Smith declared unequivocally that 'the admissible evidence was sufficient to obtain and sustain a conviction at trial' and that Trump had engaged in 'criminal efforts to retain power,' making 'specific and knowingly false claims of election fraud.' The report quoted Trump privately remarking after Biden appeared on TV 'Can you believe I lost to this f---ing guy?' and documented Trump berating Pence for being 'too honest.' Smith noted the only reason Trump escaped prosecution was DOJ's longstanding policy against prosecuting a sitting president — not the absence of evidence. Trump dismissed the report as the work of a 'lamebrain prosecutor.'

title: DOJ Indicts NY AG Letitia James; Federal Judge Dismisses Case as Unlawfully Filed
synopsis: In August 2025, the DOJ convened a grand jury and subpoenaed New York AG Letitia James' office for documents relating to her civil fraud case against Trump and her case against the NRA. On October 9, 2025 — days after Trump publicly complained on Truth Social that James had not yet been charged — the U.S. Attorney's office for the Eastern District of Virginia indicted James on mortgage fraud charges. James called it 'the most blatant example of this administration carrying out the president's political retribution campaign.' On November 24, 2025, U.S. District Judge Cameron McGowan Currie dismissed the case, ruling that the prosecutor — Trump loyalist Lindsey Halligan — had been unlawfully appointed as interim U.S. Attorney. A grand jury subsequently declined to re-indict James twice, including a second refusal on December 11, 2025.

sources.title: New York AG Letitia James indicted on fraud charge | AP News

title: Trump Threatens Military Force to Seize Greenland from Denmark
synopsis: On January 7, 2025, President-elect Trump held a press conference at Mar-a-Lago where he refused to rule out using military or economic force to acquire Greenland, saying 'We need Greenland for national security purposes' and that U.S. control was 'an absolute necessity.' He threatened to 'tariff Denmark at a very high level' if Copenhagen refused to relinquish the autonomous territory. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen held a 45-minute emergency call with Trump on January 15 and told him that 'Greenland is not for sale' and that only Greenlanders could decide their own future. The crisis triggered extraordinary cross-party meetings in Copenhagen and drew condemnation from Germany, France, and the EU, who warned the principle of inviolable borders applied to all nations.

sources.title: Trump won't rule out military force to take Greenland : NPR

title: Trump Vows to 'Take Back' Panama Canal in Inauguration Speech
synopsis: In his January 20, 2025 inauguration address, Trump invoked 19th-century 'Manifest Destiny' rhetoric and vowed that the United States would retake the Panama Canal, declaring 'We didn't give it to China. We gave it to Panama, and we're taking it back.' On February 2, Trump reiterated the threat, warning of 'powerful' U.S. action and saying 'we're going to take it back, or something very powerful is going to happen.' Panama's President Raül Mulino told Secretary of State Rubio that Panama's sovereignty over the canal was 'not up for debate.' By March 2025 Trump hailed a BlackRock deal to buy Chinese-linked ports as proof the U.S. was 'reclaiming' the canal, though Panama retained full operational sovereignty.

sources.title: Trump vows to take back Panama Canal, talks of 'Manifest Destiny' in space

title: Trump Withdraws U.S. from Paris Climate Agreement — Again
synopsis: Within hours of being sworn in on January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing immediate withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, his second such action after doing so in 2017. The order instructed the U.S. Ambassador to the UN to 'immediately submit formal written notification' of withdrawal, declaring it 'effective immediately upon notification.' The move left the United States as one of only four countries outside the agreement — alongside Iran, Libya, and Yemen — and cut off all U.S. climate finance commitments. Climate experts warned the withdrawal would embolden other nations to backslide and cede U.S. influence over global emissions policy for years.

sources.title: Trump signs order directing US withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement | AP News

title: Trump Withdraws U.S. from World Health Organization — Again
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order beginning the process of withdrawing the U.S. from the World Health Organization for the second time, stating 'World Health ripped us off, everybody rips off the United States — it's not going to happen anymore.' The withdrawal initiates a 12-month notice period and immediately halted all U.S. financial contributions; the U.S. had been funding roughly 18% of WHO's $6.8 billion biennial budget. Public health experts warned the move would undermine U.S. standing as a global health leader and impair pandemic preparedness worldwide. The action reversed Biden's 2021 re-entry and came amid an ongoing bird flu H5N1 outbreak, prompting alarm from WHO and Germany.

sources.title: Trump wants to pull the US out of the World Health Organization again. Here's what may happen next | AP News

title: Trump's 28-Point Ukraine 'Peace Plan' Demands Territorial Surrender to Russia
synopsis: In November 2025, the Trump administration circulated a 28-point peace framework for Ukraine that demanded Kyiv cede the Donbas — including territory Ukraine still controlled — to Russia, accept de facto U.S. recognition of Crimea as Russian, cut its military by more than half, and abandon NATO membership ambitions. President Zelensky responded in a nationally broadcast speech that Ukraine faced 'one of the most difficult moments in our history,' warning the country would have to choose between its 'dignity' or losing its 'key partner.' Trump set a Thanksgiving deadline for Zelensky to sign, with aides saying 'either this, or nothing.' European and Ukrainian officials called the plan 'capitulation'; Putin said it could serve as a 'basis' for settlement as it contained most of Russia's demands.

sources.title: Here's what's in the Trump administration's proposed 28-point Russia-Ukraine peace plan - CBS News

title: Trump Demands NATO Allies Pay 5% of GDP for Defense
synopsis: Throughout 2025, Trump pressed NATO allies to raise defense spending from 2% to 5% of GDP — more than double any ally's existing target — framing refusal as justification for trade retaliation. At the June 24–25, 2025 Hague Summit, allies agreed to a communiqué pledging '5% of GDP on core defense requirements by 2035,' though the language allowed holdouts like Spain to opt out. Trump publicly threatened Spain at the summit's closing: 'We're negotiating with Spain on a trade deal and will make them pay twice as much. I'm serious about that.' Prior to the summit Trump had again raised doubts about whether the U.S. would honor Article 5 collective defense, sending shockwaves through European capitals dependent on U.S. deterrence.

sources.title: NATO won't back Trump's new defence spending target but will raise its sights

title: Trump Calls Putin's Ukraine Invasion 'Genius' and 'Savvy'
synopsis: On February 22, 2022, Trump declared on radio: 'I went in yesterday and there was a television screen, and I said, This is genius. Putin declares a big portion of Ukraine as independent.' He praised Putin as 'very savvy' for framing the invasion as a 'peacekeeping' operation. Although pre-dating his second term, the statements directly shaped his second administration's pro-Russia Ukraine posture — he repeatedly cited them in office to justify refusing to condemn Putin, and no retraction was ever issued. Rep. Liz Cheney responded: 'Former President Trump's adulation of Putin today — including calling him a genius — aids our enemies.'

title: Trump Administration Pauses, Then Cuts Off U.S. Weapons to Ukraine
synopsis: In late January 2025, within days of inauguration, the Trump administration briefly halted weapons shipments to Ukraine as internal factions debated whether to end all military aid. By February 28, 2025, with 50 consecutive days having passed without any new Pentagon weapons package, the flow of U.S. arms had 'essentially stopped,' according to the New York Times. Following the Oval Office clash with Zelensky that day, a Trump official warned all U.S. aid — including shipments already authorized and paid for by Biden — could be 'canceled imminently.' On March 3, the White House formally confirmed a pause 'until Ukraine demonstrates good-faith commitment to peace,' ordered by Trump through Defense Secretary Hegseth.

sources.title: US won't send some weapons pledged to Ukraine | AP News

title: Trump-Putin Direct Phone Calls Bypass U.S. Allies on Ukraine War
synopsis: On February 12, 2025, Trump held his first post-inauguration call with Putin lasting over an hour, announcing afterward that both Putin and Zelensky 'want peace' and ordering U.S. officials to begin ceasefire talks — without NATO or European consultation. A March 18 call produced a Russian pledge to pause strikes on energy infrastructure, again announced unilaterally by Trump. On May 19, Trump announced after another call that 'Russia and Ukraine will immediately start negotiations,' though the Kremlin contradicted him, saying the process would 'take time.' By October 2025, Trump announced he would meet Putin in Budapest after a two-hour call, stunning European allies who had not been briefed, reigniting fears of capitulation to Moscow.

sources.title: In phone call with Putin, Trump abruptly ends U.S. efforts to isolate Russia | PBS News

title: Trump Declares 'Crimea Will Stay with Russia,' Endorses Russian Territorial Gains
synopsis: In an April 25, 2025 Time magazine interview, Trump stated flatly: 'Crimea will stay with Russia. Zelenskyy understands that, and everybody understands that it's been with them for a long time.' When reporters asked if Zelensky was 'ready to give up Crimea,' Trump said 'Oh, I think so,' blaming Barack Obama for the 2014 annexation. The administration's 28-point peace framework circulated in November 2025 formalized this position, calling for U.S. de facto recognition of Crimea, Luhansk, and Donetsk as Russian territory. Ukrainian officials called the position a 'red line' they would never accept, and the U.S. thus became the first Western government to endorse Russia's illegal annexation.

sources.title: 'Crimea will stay with Russia,' Trump says as he seeks end to war in Ukraine | PBS News

title: Trump Uses Tariff Threats to Coerce Allies Over Greenland, Canada, NATO
synopsis: At his January 7, 2025 Mar-a-Lago press conference, Trump announced he would impose tariffs on Denmark 'at a very high level' unless it surrendered Greenland, threatened 25% tariffs on Canada unless it became the 51st state, and promised 'very serious tariffs on Mexico and Canada' over migration. The deployment of trade leverage against allied democracies to achieve territorial and political goals — rather than legitimate trade complaints — marked an unprecedented weaponization of economic coercion. At the June 2025 NATO summit Trump threatened Spain with double tariffs for refusing to hit the 5% GDP defense spending target. European officials described the tactic as treating the entire Western alliance as a protection racket.

sources.title: European leaders warn Trump's Greenland tariffs threaten ‘dangerous downward spiral’ : NPR

title: Trump Refuses to Commit to Defending Taiwan, Abandons Strategic Clarity
synopsis: On February 26, 2025, during a White House Cabinet meeting, Trump flatly refused to answer whether the U.S. would prevent China from taking Taiwan by force, saying: 'I never comment on that. I don't want to ever put myself in that position.' The statement reversed the Biden administration's explicit 'strategic clarity' commitment to defend Taiwan and returned the U.S. to strategic ambiguity. Trump had already told Bloomberg Businessweek that Taiwan 'should pay the U.S. for defense' and that 'Taiwan doesn't give us anything.' Analysts noted that Trump's framing — demanding Taiwan pay for protection like an insurance client — signaled that the defense commitment was for sale, alarming Taipei and prompting Taiwan to pledge increased investment and defense spending.

sources.title: Trump mum on U.S. defending Taiwan from China

title: Trump Withdraws U.S. from UN Human Rights Council — Again
synopsis: On February 4, 2025, Trump signed an executive order withdrawing the U.S. from the UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC), repeating his 2018 action that Biden had reversed in 2021. The order declared the UNHRC 'attacks our allies and propagates anti-Semitism,' terminated the U.S. Representative's office, and cut all U.S. funding to the body. The withdrawal came the same day Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu visited the White House — the first foreign leader Trump hosted in his second term — signaling the move was directly tied to shielding Israel from Council scrutiny during the Gaza conflict. The order also cut funding to UNRWA, the main UN relief agency for Palestinians, despite an independent review finding no evidence to substantiate Israeli accusations that UNRWA staff participated in the October 7 attacks.

sources.title: Trump announces withdrawal from UN human rights body and halt to funding for Palestinian refugees

title: Trump Sanctions ICC to Shield Israel, Threatening International Justice System
synopsis: On February 6, 2025, Trump signed an executive order imposing IEEPA-based sanctions on ICC officials investigating Israel, authorizing asset freezes and U.S. entry bans on ICC prosecutors, employees, and their 'immediate family members.' The order accused the Court of 'illegitimate and baseless actions targeting America and our close ally Israel' over arrest warrants for Israeli PM Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Gallant for war crimes. On July 18, 2025 a federal judge blocked enforcement, ruling the order was an unconstitutional infringement on free speech. The ICC sanctions effectively sought to criminalize international human rights lawyers, NGOs, and banks providing routine services to the Court, extending Trump's legal war against international accountability institutions.

sources.title: Trump signs order imposing sanctions on International Criminal Court over investigations of Israel | AP News

title: USAID Shutdown Kills Hundreds of Thousands, Ends Lifesaving Programs Worldwide
synopsis: Beginning January 20, 2025, the Trump administration froze all foreign aid for 90 days, then terminated more than 90% of USAID contracts — cutting $60 billion in global assistance and dismantling programs covering HIV/AIDS treatment for 2.3 million people, malaria prevention, maternal health, and famine response across Africa, Afghanistan, Yemen, and beyond. A Center for Global Development study published in December 2025 estimated the cuts could contribute to between 500,000 and 1.6 million additional deaths annually. On the ground, BBC and CNN documented maternal deaths in Afghanistan after 400+ medical clinics closed, spiking malaria mortality in northern Cameroon due to antimalarial supply chain collapse, and in Nigeria a twin infant died of malnutrition after Mercy Corps abruptly ended its therapeutic feeding program when its USAID contract was canceled. The Trump administration publicly insisted 'no one has died because of aid cuts.'

sources.title: The USAID shutdown is upending lives for thousands in US | AP News

title: Trump's Day-One Immigration Executive Order Blitz
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, President Trump signed a cascade of executive orders declaring a national emergency at the southern border, directing the Pentagon to deploy troops and provide detention space, and shutting down the CBP One app — instantly canceling existing appointment slots for hundreds of thousands of migrants. Additional orders suspended the refugee resettlement program for 120 days, terminated Biden-era humanitarian parole programs for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans, reinstated mandatory detention pending removal, and ordered immediate restart of border wall construction. The ten-plus executive actions marked the most sweeping first-day immigration crackdown in modern U.S. history, triggering immediate federal court challenges across multiple circuits.

sources.title: Trump's Day 1 executive actions | PBS News

title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia: Wrongly Deported to CECOT, Supreme Court Orders Return
synopsis: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration deported Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia — a Salvadoran man who had legally lived in Maryland for a decade with a work permit and no criminal record — to El Salvador's notorious CECOT mega-prison, in explicit violation of a 2019 immigration court 'withholding order' barring his removal there. The government acknowledged the deportation was an 'administrative error.' District Judge Paula Xinis ordered his return by April 7; the Supreme Court unanimously upheld the order on April 10 (Noem v. Abrego Garcia), requiring the government to 'facilitate' his return. Despite the Supreme Court ruling, the Trump administration for months refused to take meaningful steps to secure his release from CECOT, with officials arguing U.S. courts lacked jurisdiction once he crossed the border — a position Justice Sotomayor called an argument for unchecked power to deport even U.S. citizens.

sources.title: Who is Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the man ICE mistakenly deported? | AP News

title: ICE Ends 'Sensitive Locations' Protections: Arrests at Churches, Schools, Hospitals
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman rescinded the Obama-era 2011 'sensitive locations' policy, which had prohibited ICE and CBP from making immigration arrests at schools, hospitals, churches, and other protected sites. A January 31 ICE memo renamed the rescission 'Common Sense Enforcement Actions,' giving field officers case-by-case discretion with no categorical protections. The move immediately spread fear in immigrant communities, with some families pulling children from school. A federal court in March 2025 issued an injunction requiring ICE to follow the old guidelines at approximately 1,400 listed houses of worship across 36 states in cases lacking a valid warrant — but protections for schools, hospitals, and other sensitive venues remained eliminated nationwide.

sources.title: Trump administration throws out policies limiting arrests of migrants at sensitive locations | AP News

title: Family Separation 2.0: 205,000 Children Lose a Parent to Deportation
synopsis: Unlike the border-based 'zero tolerance' separations of Trump's first term that affected roughly 5,000 children, the second term's family separations played out invisibly across U.S. communities. A July 2025 ICE directive rescinded Biden-era protections against detaining parents of U.S.-citizen children and abolished requirements to place detained parents near their minor children. The Brookings Institution estimated approximately 205,000 children — 71 percent of them U.S. citizens — had a parent detained by immigration officials as of May 2026; CNN identified over 100 U.S.-citizen children left stranded without parents by September 2025. ORR shared over 460,000 tips about unaccompanied children with ICE, leading to more than 12,000 arrests of child sponsors.

title: Alien Enemies Act Invoked for Venezuelan Gang Members, Flights Defy Court Order
synopsis: On March 15, 2025, President Trump invoked the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 — last used during World War II — against Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang members, declaring them 'alien enemies' subject to summary deportation without due process or immigration court review. Hours after the proclamation, U.S. District Judge James Boasberg issued an emergency restraining order halting the deportations and ordering planes already in the air to return; the administration defiantly continued the flights, claiming the planes had already left U.S. airspace. Over 261 people were deported to El Salvador's CECOT prison, including 101 who were not charged with any gang activity but deported simply for being undocumented. The brazen defiance of a federal court order triggered a constitutional crisis, with legal scholars warning the administration's position would allow the government to deport anyone, including U.S. citizens, without court review.

sources.title: Judge bars deportations of Venezuelans from South Texas under 18th-century Alien Enemies Act | PBS News

title: CECOT: El Salvador's Torture Prison Becomes U.S. Immigration Detention Partner
synopsis: Starting March 16, 2025, the Trump administration began paying El Salvador $20,000 per inmate per year to house U.S. deportees in CECOT, the Terrorism Confinement Center, a maximum-security facility where inmates have their heads shaved, are kept in communal cells of up to 100 men for 23.5 hours per day on metal bunks with no mattresses, with no visitation, education, or recreation permitted. Human rights organizations condemned the arrangement as a potential violation of international law's non-refoulement principle and the Convention Against Torture. By July 2025, El Salvador acknowledged to UN investigators that the Trump administration maintained 'exclusive jurisdiction and legal responsibility' over the CECOT detainees. At least 101 of the 261 initial deportees had no alleged gang ties, having been sent there simply for being in the U.S. without documentation.

sources.title: What to know about the El Salvador mega-prison where Trump sent deported Venezuelans

title: ICE Detains Over 170 U.S. Citizens During Immigration Raids
synopsis: A ProPublica investigation published October 2025 documented more than 170 incidents during Trump's second administration in which U.S. citizens were detained by immigration agents — overwhelmingly Latino. Cases included combat veteran George Retes, held three days without a phone call after a California raid; Florida-born construction worker Leonardo Garcia Venegas, detained twice in Alabama despite showing a valid REAL ID; and Albuquerque resident Jose Hermosillo, held 10 days in an Arizona detention facility. Most strikingly, Alma Bowman of Macon, Georgia, a 59-year-old U.S. citizen, spent 243 days at Stewart Detention Center before being released without a court order. In over 20 cases, citizens were held incommunicado for more than a day; nearly all detained U.S. citizens were Latino.

sources.title: Democrats to Investigate Immigration Agents Detaining of American Citizens — ProPublica

title: Military Deployed to Southern Border as Domestic Law Enforcement, Posse Comitatus Sidestepped
synopsis: By mid-2025, Trump had tripled U.S. troop deployments at the southern border to over 8,600 active-duty soldiers including 4th Infantry Division Stryker combat vehicles, helicopters, and surveillance drones — at a cost exceeding $525 million. To sidestep the Posse Comitatus Act of 1878, Trump designated hundreds of thousands of acres of federal land in New Mexico and Texas as 'National Defense Areas,' effectively converting stretches of the border into military installations where soldiers could detain civilians accused of trespassing. By June 11, 2025, U.S. troops began directly detaining migrants; over 1,400 migrants were charged federally with 'unauthorized entry into a military zone.' Legal experts warned this represented the most aggressive expansion of military domestic enforcement authority in the post-Civil War era.

sources.title: US military's expanded new role on US-Mexico border raises questions | AP News

title: Birthright Citizenship Executive Order Blocked by Four Courts
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to refuse to recognize U.S. citizenship for children born on U.S. soil if neither parent is a citizen or lawful permanent resident — a direct challenge to the 14th Amendment's citizenship clause, settled law since United States v. Wong Kim Ark (1898). Federal judges blocked the order within days; three separate courts issued nationwide injunctions in early 2025. The 9th Circuit ruled the order unconstitutional on July 23, 2025, and the 1st Circuit upheld a nationwide injunction on October 3, 2025. The Supreme Court's June 27, 2025 ruling limiting 'universal injunctions' complicated enforcement of the blocks without overturning them, leaving the order universally suspended as of August 2026.

sources.title: Fourth court blocks Trump's birthright citizenship order nationwide

title: Remain in Mexico Reinstated, Asylum Effectively Ended at the Border
synopsis: On January 20–21, 2025, the Trump administration reinstated the Migrant Protection Protocols (MPP) via Executive Order 14165 and a DHS directive, requiring non-Mexican asylum seekers to return to Mexico while U.S. cases are adjudicated — replicating a policy that during Trump's first term left tens of thousands of asylum seekers stranded in dangerous Mexican border cities for years, exposed to kidnapping and extortion by cartels. Simultaneously, the administration terminated the CBP One app, ended categorical parole programs for 530,000 Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans, and suspended the refugee admissions program. Combined with near-zero asylum eligibility, the measures effectively ended almost all legal pathways to asylum in the United States. Courts would block some elements, but the aggregate effect was to reduce legal border crossings to near-zero.

sources.title: Trump administration says it is reinstating 'remain in Mexico' program

title: Deportation Flights to Libya, Colombia, Guatemala — Third-Country Removals Expand
synopsis: Beginning January 27, 2025, the Trump administration conducted military deportation flights to Guatemala (the first country to accept C-17 cargo planes with shackled migrants), triggering a near-trade-war with Colombia after President Gustavo Petro refused to accept U.S. military aircraft on January 26 — forcing Trump to threaten 25% tariffs before Colombia relented. By May 6–7, 2025, the administration announced plans to deport migrants to Libya — a country racked by civil conflict whose migrant detention centers human rights groups have called 'horrific' — despite migrants having no connection to Libya; a federal judge blocked the flights absent a chance for migrants to contest the move. The program represented an unprecedented expansion of 'third-country removals' to nations with documented human rights violations, raising serious questions under international non-refoulement obligations.

sources.title: Judge blocks deportation flight of Asian migrants to Libya

title: Sanctuary City Raids: 'Operation Midway Blitz' and Nationwide ICE Sweeps
synopsis: The Trump administration conducted targeted, high-profile ICE operations in cities with sanctuary policies, deploying Border Patrol agents, the National Guard, and other federal forces alongside ICE. In the Chicago area, 'Operation Midway Blitz' launched in September 2025 resulted in over 1,000 arrests within weeks; AP documented agents storming an apartment complex by helicopter as families slept and deploying chemical agents near a public school. Data from the Deportation Data Project showed that in these high-profile sanctuary-city operations, more than half of those arrested had no criminal record — compared to a third nationally — directly contradicting the administration's stated focus on dangerous criminals. New York City saw 1,900+ arrests in early months, while Los Angeles saw a 69% jump and Miami 161%.

sources.title: Feds say more than 1,500 arrested in "Operation Midway Blitz," but data reveals some arrests from outside Illinois - CBS Chicago

title: Pro-Palestinian Students Targeted: Mahmoud Khalil, Rumeysa Ozturk Detained
synopsis: The Trump administration launched a systematic campaign to arrest, detain, and deport foreign students who participated in pro-Palestinian demonstrations, citing a rarely-used 1952 INA provision allowing expulsion of noncitizens whose presence is 'detrimental to U.S. foreign policy interests.' Mahmoud Khalil, a Palestinian Columbia University graduate and green card holder with no criminal record, was arrested by ICE agents in his university apartment on March 8, 2025 — with an agent revoking his green card over the phone in real time. On March 25, Rumeysa Ozturk, a Turkish doctoral student at Tufts, was detained on a suburban Boston street; DHS alleged without evidence she 'supported Hamas.' An immigration judge ruled on April 11 that Khalil could be deported; out of approximately 5,000 pro-Palestinian protesters investigated, 18 were arrested, but the chilling effect on academic freedom was immediate and severe.

sources.title: Lawmakers visit Mahmoud Khalil, Rümeysa Öztürk in Louisiana jail

title: Legal Immigration Systematically Dismantled: H-1B $100K Fee, Student Visas Halved
synopsis: While publicly claiming to support legal immigration, the Trump administration in 2025–2026 implemented the most comprehensive suppression of legal immigration in modern U.S. history. In September 2025 Trump imposed a $100,000 fee on H-1B visa sponsorships, effectively pricing out small employers; the State Department in January 2026 suspended issuance of permanent visas for 75 countries accounting for 46% of all immigrant visas; student (F-1) visa issuance fell by almost half in 2025; USCIS paused green card processing for refugees and asylees 'for additional vetting'; and travel bans were imposed on nationals of 39 countries. synopsis: Trump's June 2025 annual financial disclosure revealed that Dar Al Arkan — a publicly traded Saudi real estate developer chaired by Yousef Al Shelash — paid the Trump Organization $21.9 million in brand license fees in 2024 for luxury tower projects in Dubai and Oman, plus an additional $5.35 million in related payments. title: Kushner Affinity Partners Grows to $4.8B as Gulf Sovereign Funds Pour In During Trump Presidency
synopsis: Jared Kushner's private equity firm Affinity Partners — founded six months after he left the White House — grew to $4.8 billion in assets under management by March 2025, up from $3 billion the prior year, driven by new $1.5 billion commitments from Abu Dhabi-based Lunate and the Qatar Investment Authority. The Saudi Public Investment Fund had originally invested $2 billion in 2021 despite its own screening panel citing Kushner's 'inexperience,' 'unsatisfactory' due diligence results, and 'public relations risks' from his White House role; the PIF board overruled the panel. As of a September 2024 Senate Finance Committee report, Affinity had collected at least $112 million in management fees while returning zero profits to investors — prompting Senator Ron Wyden to question whether the fund was structured primarily to pay the Kushner family rather than generate returns. The expansion of Gulf investment accelerated in direct proportion to Trump's return to power.

title: Mar-a-Lago Membership Raised to $1 Million as Access to the President Becomes Marketable

The club, capped at approximately 500 members, offers direct physical access to Trump and visiting dignitaries in an unvetted social setting; during Trump's first term, members influenced policy through informal access and memos scrawled on cocktail napkins. Annual dues run approximately $22,750 atop the initiation fee, generating an estimated $24 million or more annually. Ethics watchdogs noted that the club's membership structure functionally sells proximity to the presidency at a price set by the president himself, with no disclosure requirements for who is buying memberships or what they are seeking from the administration.

title: Eric and Donald Trump Jr. Sign Billions in Foreign Deals Weeks Before Trump Gulf State Visit
synopsis: In late April and early May 2025, Trump's sons Eric and Donald Trump Jr. conducted a global deal blitz across the Middle East and Europe — announcing a Trump International Hotel & Tower in Dubai with Dar Global (an 80-story tower with $20 million penthouses), a second Trump Tower in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and a luxury golf resort in Doha in partnership with Qatari Diar, the real estate arm of Qatar's sovereign wealth fund. The Trump Organization's 2025 ethics white paper allowed all foreign private company deals, unlike the first-term agreement. title: One Big Beautiful Bill: Trump's Businesses and Estate Stand to Save Hundreds of Millions
synopsis: Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on July 4, 2025, locking in $3.4 trillion in tax cuts over ten years — with the top 1 percent of earners projected by ITEP to receive $1.02 trillion of those cuts over a decade. Key provisions directly benefit Trump personally: the 20% pass-through deduction (now permanent at 23%) reduces the effective tax rate on Trump Organization revenues to roughly 29.6%, the estate and gift tax exemption was permanently raised to $15 million per individual/$30 million per couple (preventing hundreds of millions in eventual estate taxes on Trump's properties), and 100% bonus depreciation was made permanent (allowing immediate write-offs on real estate and equipment). The legislation was drafted and signed by a president who refused to place his assets in a blind trust, creating a textbook self-dealing scenario in which Trump championed — and personally benefited from — his own signature legislation.

title: Trump Pardons Campaign Donors Facing Federal Fraud and Corruption Convictions

title: Foreign Governments Book Trump Hotels to Curry Favor — Second-Term Pattern Resumes
synopsis: During Trump's first term, congressional investigators documented at least $13.6 million in payments from 20 foreign governments to Trump properties, with the largest flows from China ($5.57M), Qatar ($1.1M), and Saudi Arabia ($885K); the constitutional Foreign Emoluments Clause requires congressional approval for any such payments. For his second term, Trump made no structural changes: he retained full ownership of the Trump Organization and adopted an ethics white paper that permitted private foreign company deals while pledging only to donate profits from government patronage — a methodology CREW found to have covered less than 4% of actual first-term foreign government payments. Countries previously found to have targeted Trump properties — including Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Turkey, Malaysia, and China — all had active diplomatic and policy agendas with the Trump administration in 2025, and all owned or regularly rented units or event space in Trump-branded properties.

title: RFK Jr. Cites Fraudulent Vaccine-Autism Paper at Senate Confirmation Hearing
synopsis: During his January 29–30, 2025 Senate HELP Committee confirmation hearing for HHS Secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. refused to state that vaccines do not cause autism, despite overwhelming scientific consensus. When Republican Chairman Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana presented a 2014 meta-analysis of 1.2 million children finding zero vaccine-autism link, Kennedy deflected, then cited a fatally flawed January 2025 paper by researcher Mawson published in Science, Public Health Policy and the Law — a journal not indexed on PubMed or MEDLINE. The study claimed vaccinated Florida Medicaid children were 2.7 times more likely to develop autism, but epidemiologists identified severe confounding, ignored all contra-evidence, and noted it cited a previously retracted paper. Kennedy declared he would follow the science while citing junk science. The original 1998 Wakefield study that sparked vaccine-autism concerns had already been retracted as fraudulent. Cassidy stated he was struggling with Kennedy's nomination before ultimately voting to confirm him. The episode signaled Kennedy's intent to use HHS to promote long-debunked anti-vaccine theories as official policy.

title: RFK Jr. Declares Autism Epidemic Caused by Environmental Toxin, Distorts All Science
synopsis: On April 16, 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. held a press conference announcing new CDC autism prevalence data and declared autism a preventable epidemic caused by an unidentified environmental toxin. Kennedy contradicted established science on multiple fronts: he falsely stated that 75–85% of the observed increase in autism rates was real rather than attributable to broader diagnostic criteria, citing a retracted 2014 paper as support. FactCheck.org documented that Kennedy mischaracterized a 1970 Wisconsin study and in a later April 22 Fox News interview falsely claimed all the kids in Wisconsin were tested. Kennedy also falsely invoked a paper that had been retracted nearly two years prior, claiming autism costs would reach $1 trillion a year by 2035. Meanwhile, his agency eliminated NIOSH divisions studying environmental links to autism and canceled over $40 million in NIH autism research grants. ProPublica reported that Kennedy was simultaneously gutting the scientific infrastructure he claimed to need. His September deadline to identify the autism cause passed without results, as he later acknowledged his timeline was overly optimistic.

title: Trump Invokes Alien Enemies Act with False Invasion Claim About Tren de Aragua
synopsis: On March 15, 2025, President Trump issued a proclamation invoking the 1798 Alien Enemies Act to deport Venezuelan nationals, declaring that the gang Tren de Aragua had irrefutably invaded the United States. Legal and immigration experts immediately noted the claim was legally and factually false: the Constitution's invasion requirement refers to armed military attack by a foreign nation, not criminal gang activity. Constitutional law professors including Mary Ellen O'Connell of Notre Dame and Matthew Lindsay of the University of Baltimore noted Trump's usage contradicted all historical and legal interpretations. The proclamation contradicted itself by claiming Tren de Aragua was both a quasi-independent government and an agent of the Venezuelan Maduro regime simultaneously. In Aurora, Colorado — which Trump had called overrun by the gang — local police identified just over a dozen alleged gang members in a city of 395,000. NPR reporting found a subsequent August 2025 DOJ indictment of 30 people involved mostly old cases opened under Biden, with investigators loosely identifying gang membership via tattoos alone. Of the 30 arrested, only 8 were classified as gang members, and 2 of those were in Colombia at the time of arrest.

title: Trump Falsely Claims $88 Billion in Tariff Revenue in Two Months
synopsis: On June 11, 2025, President Trump told reporters at the Kennedy Center that the U.S. had brought in $88 billion in tariffs in two months, far beyond what anybody expected. He repeated the claim the following day at a White House bill signing. FactCheck.org investigation found the claim false: actual tariff revenue from the entire October 2024–May 2025 fiscal year totaled $81.4 billion — a period that included over three months when Biden was still president. No two-month period came close to $88 billion. Trump also claimed he had attracted $9 trillion in new U.S. investments — a figure the White House's own webpage listed as $5 trillion as of April 29, and $9.6 trillion by December 10. Economists noted the list included unverified pledges and pre-existing Biden-era investments recategorized under Trump. CBS News confirmed several listed investments had been announced before Trump's reelection. In a December 9 rally, Trump had inflated the investment total to $18 trillion, more than double the White House's own tally. Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell cited tariff uncertainty and forecast meaningful inflation increases. Trump responded by questioning whether Powell was a Democrat.

title: Tom Homan Spreads Misleading 600,000 Criminal Immigrants Statistic
synopsis: Beginning July 7, 2025, Trump's border czar Tom Homan repeatedly claimed at public events — including the Turning Point USA Student Action Summit on July 12 and on Fox News — that over 600,000 illegal aliens with criminal records were walking the streets of this nation. FactCheck.org documented extensive flaws: the 647,572 figure from a 2024 ICE letter to Congress included legal immigrants, not just undocumented ones; approximately one-third (222,141) had only been charged, not convicted; roughly 126,000 had only traffic offenses and 92,000 had only immigration offenses; the data spanned 40-plus years of entrants, not recent arrivals; and an undetermined number were already incarcerated by other agencies. Trump himself had separately claimed Biden let in 13,099 convicted murderers, then shifted to 11,888 murderers — numbers drawn from the same dataset but excluding the 40-year timeframe caveat. Reuters data showed ICE detentions of people with no criminal charges jumped 800% under Trump, from approximately 860 in January to 7,800 by June 2025, undercutting the crime-focused messaging.

title: FBI Director Kash Patel Promotes Unverified CCP 2020 Election Conspiracy Theory
synopsis: On June 17, 2025, FBI Director Kash Patel published a post claiming the FBI had located alarming documents alleging Chinese Communist Party interference in the 2020 election. Patel said he had immediately declassified the material and shared it with Sen. Chuck Grassley. The documents centered on an unverified 2020 tip from an anonymous confidential informant claiming China mass-produced fake driver's licenses for a mail-in ballot scheme. NBC News and election law experts noted the tip was never substantiated: the only evidence Patel cited was CBP seizures of fake IDs from China, which CBP itself attributed to underage college students seeking to purchase alcohol. Election law expert Rick Hasen said Patel's post might feed the MAGA base but amounted to promoting an uncorroborated story of unknown origin with no evidence that anything actually happened. Two former senior FBI officials noted the bureau receives hundreds of tips daily, many unverified, and one warned that publicizing this information played into the hands of our foreign enemies. No evidence of widespread 2020 voter fraud has been found by any investigation, including those conducted by Trump-appointed officials.

title: Gabbard Declares Obama Treasonous Conspiracy Based on Misrepresented Intelligence
synopsis: On July 17–18, 2025, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard held a White House briefing room press conference and released declassified documents she claimed proved a treasonous conspiracy by Obama administration officials who manufactured and politicized intelligence against Trump. Gabbard submitted criminal referrals to the Justice Department. AP News, PolitiFact, and multiple national security lawyers examined the documents and found that Gabbard's core claim — that the intelligence community reversed a no Russian interference finding at Obama's political direction — was not supported by the material she released. The documents showed routine intelligence review processes, not conspiracy. The 2020 bipartisan Senate Intelligence Committee report, signed by Marco Rubio (now Trump's Secretary of State), had already found irrefutable evidence of Russian meddling. National security lawyer Bradley Moss characterized Gabbard's narrative as targeting an issue that was not ultimately the focus of those analyses. Democratic lawmakers noted the treasonous conspiracy framing emerged simultaneously with growing MAGA fury over the Epstein files, suggesting political deflection.

title: Trump Accuses Obama of Treason and Coup in Oval Office Remarks
synopsis: On July 20–22, 2025, President Trump publicly accused former President Barack Obama of treason — a charge carrying the death penalty — and claimed Obama had been trying to lead a coup with Hillary Clinton in 2016. Trump made the accusation during an Oval Office meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. PolitiFact rated the claim False: a coup would have required Obama to prevent Trump from taking office, which he explicitly did not do — Obama facilitated the 2016 transition and acknowledged Trump's victory. George Mason University law professor Ilya Somin noted that unlike Trump's own actions leading to January 6, Obama in 2016 acknowledged his party lost the election and facilitated rather than impeded the peaceful transition of power. Trump based his accusations on Gabbard's contested declassification. John Durham's three-year special counsel investigation had already found no criminal conspiracy by Obama officials. Legal experts noted both statutes of limitations and the Supreme Court's 2024 presidential immunity decision would likely shield Obama even if the claims were valid. Obama spokesperson Patrick Rodenbush called the claims bizarre and ridiculous.

title: Trump Posts AI Deepfake Video of Barack Obama Being Arrested in Oval Office
synopsis: On July 20, 2025, President Trump shared an AI-generated video on Truth Social depicting former President Barack Obama being handcuffed and dragged to the floor by FBI agents in the Oval Office as Trump smiled, then shown in an orange prison jumpsuit behind bars. The video, set to the Village People's YMCA, was first posted to TikTok — where it received over 420,000 views — before Trump reshared it. The White House issued no correction or disclaimer; Deputy Press Secretary Harrison Fields defended the post by claiming President Trump was right about the Obama-Biden administration's clear involvement in the greatest witch hunt in American history. The incident occurred two days after Gabbard's criminal referral to DOJ. No credible news outlet reported any actual arrest of Obama. AP News confirmed the video was entirely AI-fabricated. PolitiFact's October 2025 analysis found that Trump had shared at least 36 AI posts since his inauguration, roughly half promoting his image and 12 degrading opponents, with the White House stating the memes will continue. The administration thereby normalized the use of fabricated deepfake content as official political communication.

title: DOJ and FBI Spend Months Investigating Epstein QAnon Client List Conspiracy
synopsis: In early 2025, the Trump administration directed the FBI and Justice Department to conduct what became a months-long investigation into the QAnon-rooted conspiracy theory that a secret Jeffrey Epstein client list exposing elite Democrats was being suppressed. Trump had repeatedly promised to release Epstein files during his 2024 campaign. FBI Director Kash Patel and Deputy Director Dan Bongino had spent years on podcasts winking at QAnon theorists and demanding the files' release. The Washington Post reported in July 2025 that the administration assigned government workers and spent taxpayer dollars to address conspiracy theories and easily disproven assertions. On July 11, the DOJ concluded its investigation by announcing there was no incriminating client list and that Epstein had died by suicide — conclusions affirmed by prior investigations. Trump then posted on Truth Social urging supporters to stop talking about Epstein. A former Project Veritas leader at a Turning Point USA conference declared Trump had become the deep state. Russell Muirhead of Dartmouth noted that nobody exploited those questions more than Donald Trump — but now his own appointees bore the institutional credibility cost.

title: AG Pam Bondi Orders Grand Jury Probe of Obama Officials Based on Debunked Claims
synopsis: On August 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi directed Justice Department prosecutors to launch a grand jury investigation into whether Obama administration officials committed federal crimes by conducting a 2016–2017 assessment of Russian election interference. Bondi acted on Gabbard's criminal referral. A former senior DOJ official condemned the move as a dangerous political stunt. NBC News reported that Democratic lawmakers accused the administration of seeking to distract from the Epstein case fallout, as conservative media pressure over Epstein had intensified in the same period. The bipartisan 2020 Senate Intelligence Committee report signed by Rubio had already found significant Russian interference and no Obama criminal conspiracy. Special Counsel John Durham's three-year investigation under Trump's first term had also found no criminal conspiracy by Obama officials. AP News reported that Trump had made no secret of his desire to use the Justice Department as a weapon of retribution against perceived political adversaries. title: Trump Shares AI-Generated MedBed QAnon Conspiracy Video on Truth Social
synopsis: On September 27–28, 2025, President Trump posted an AI-generated video on Truth Social depicting a fake Fox News segment hosted by Lara Trump in which an AI-rendered version of Trump announced the opening of the world's first MedBed hospital and a national MedBed card system. The medbed conspiracy theory — claiming a suppressed Tesla-based technology can cure all diseases — had originated in QAnon circles and spread through fringe health communities. Fox News confirmed to multiple outlets that the segment never aired on Fox News Channel or any other Fox News Media platforms. The Verge and CNN confirmed the video was entirely AI-generated, including the depiction of Trump himself. Trump provided no explanatory text and deleted the post without comment after the fabrication was widely reported. CNN noted the deletion without explanation was characteristic of Trump's pattern: many of the president's followers acknowledged the video was AI-generated, but still seemed to believe that Trump was confirming the existence of MedBeds. PolitiFact's October 2025 survey found the MedBed post was one of 36 identified AI posts on Trump's Truth Social since January 2025, confirming a systematic pattern of synthetic media use for political messaging.

title: White House Systematically Deploys AI Deepfakes as Official Government Communications
synopsis: Beginning in early 2025, the Trump White House formally adopted AI-generated deepfakes and synthetic media as standard government communications tools. PolitiFact's October 2025 analysis documented 36 AI posts from Trump's Truth Social since inauguration, with the White House X account and DHS also regularly publishing AI-fabricated imagery. The White House posted on X on July 11, 2025: Nowhere in the Constitution does it say we can't post banger memes. The memes will continue. House Speaker Mike Johnson defended the practice as satire.

title: RFK Jr. Directs CDC to Rewrite Website Falsely Claiming Vaccines May Cause Autism
synopsis: On November 19–20, 2025, RFK Jr. personally directed the CDC to rewrite its vaccine safety webpage, replacing the long-standing scientific consensus with language stating: The claim vaccines do not cause autism is not an evidence-based claim because studies have not ruled out the possibility that infant vaccines cause autism. The page further claimed health authorities had ignored studies supporting a link. AP News, Reuters, NBC News, and the Washington Post reported widespread outrage from public health experts, autism researchers, the World Health Organization, and dozens of medical societies. Sen. Bill Cassidy — who had voted to confirm Kennedy after Kennedy promised not to undermine vaccine confidence — posted that Kennedy's action was wrong, irresponsible, and actively makes Americans sicker. Kennedy later told the New York Times he had personally directed the change. The CDC's own cited Danish 2025 study of 1.2 million children actually found aluminum in vaccines was not associated with neurodevelopmental disorders — the opposite of what the page implied. Critics noted the CDC cherry-picked discredited studies while omitting the 2015 and 2021 analyses most directly rebutting the vaccine-autism claim. The WHO reissued its statement affirming vaccines do not cause autism.

title: Trump Systematically Fabricates Economic Statistics Across 2025 Rally Speeches
synopsis: Throughout 2025, President Trump delivered a pattern of provably false economic statistics, documented across multiple FactCheck.org and AP News analyses. At a December 9 Pennsylvania rally, Trump falsely claimed he had inherited the worst inflation in the history of our country — in fact the worst post-WWI inflation occurred after World War I — and that inflation had stopped, when BLS showed 3% inflation for the 12 months ending September 2025. He claimed gasoline was at $1.99 in three or four states when no statewide average was below $2.37. He claimed 4,000 new Pennsylvania manufacturing jobs when national manufacturing employment was down 49,000. In March 2025, Trump falsely claimed he was presiding over a brand-new domestic manufacturing boom after major collapse under Biden, when manufacturing jobs rose by 610,000 under Biden's full term. He cherry-picked Biden's final year loss of 111,000 manufacturing jobs while ignoring the four-year net gain. In June 2025, Trump claimed $88 billion in tariffs in two months when the accurate figure spanned 8 months and included Biden's tenure. AP News concluded Trump's glowing account of progress under his watch was out of tune with the experience of price-squeezed Americans and the story told by some of his government's own statistics.
